_: #4265 — the language-neutral record of the futures-card caption chain.
Web resolves the caption in `frontend/components/discover/utils.ts`
(`feedContextSnippet`); iOS resolves it in
`ios/Bain Luck/Bain Luck/Utilities/DiscoverCaption.swift` (`feedCaption`).
The two can never meet inside one process, so they meet here: each side
asserts in its own runner that it reproduces every row below, and
`frontend/e2e/contract/discoverCaptionChainParity.contract.test.js` parses
the Swift table out of `DiscoverCaptionParityTests.swift` and asserts it
equals this file. Same construction as the CAL-P043 calibration record.
ORDER (web's, adopted for both): context_summary -> headline -> reason ->
hook_description -> empty. `reason` restates the market name, which the
card already prints as its title ('Los Angeles Dodgers (31%) leads MLB
World Series Winner' under a heading that reads 'MLB World Series
Winner'); `headline` is the same fact without the repetition ('Los Angeles
Dodgers leads at 31%'). UX-P045 promoted `reason` above `headline` for
SETTLED EVENTS, where `headline` is a bucket label — that precedent does
not carry to futures and this record is futures-only.
EMPTY IS ABSENT. The wire sends '' far more often than null: measured on
`GET /api/feed?limit=250`, 2026-09-09 ~07:20 PT, 113 futures cards carried
`context_summary` = '' on 23 and `reason` = '' on 23, while `headline` was
the one that arrived null (19). Web's `||` already treats '' as absent;
iOS's `??` did not, so an empty first rung won the whole chain and three
cards rendered with no caption at all. Every row whose name starts
'prod-' is one of those real cards.
